title: terraform(private): unify state layout + GPU node pools, IAM & networking modules
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Unifies Terraform state layout for private deployments; adds modular GPU node-pool, IAM and networking components. Requires state migration (see notes).
description:
Summary: This PR unifies the Terraform state layout used by the private deployment modules and introduces a set of focused modules for GPU node pools, IAM roles/policies, and VPC networking primitives. Motivation: private/private-installer and our on-prem customers have had divergent state layouts and module boundaries which made upgrades, drift correction, and cross-account reuse error-prone. Unifying the state layout and splitting responsibilities into smaller modules enables safer rollouts, more predictable state migrations, and reuse across multiple private clusters (air-gapped / VPC).

What this changes (high-level):
- Introduces modules/gpu-node-pool (GKE/AKS/EKS wrappers) with clear input/output contract and tagging conventions.
- Introduces modules/iam-private with least-privilege role templates for node pools, controller services and KMS integrations.
- Introduces modules/networking-private which centralizes VPC/subnet/route table management and exposes interfaces for shared and dedicated networking.
- Reworks root state layout: moves resource groups into nested state per-environment (env/<env>/...) and adds state locking conventions for multi-team ownership.
- Adds a migration helper script scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh and documentation in docs/priv-deploy/state-migration.md.

Commits (summary):
- 1a2b3c4: initial split: add gpu-node-pool, iam-private, networking-private modules
- 2b3c4d5: refactor root module to use new module inputs and update examples
- 3c4d5e6: add state migration helper and checklist
- 4d5e6f7: tighten IAM policy scopes and add integration tests for role assumption
- 5e6f7g8: update README, add upgrade notes and changelog

Files changed (selected):
- modules/gpu-node-pool/main.tf (new) -- creates node pool resources, autoscaling config, taints/labels
- modules/iam-private/roles.tf (new) -- node role, controller role, kms-encrypt role with minimized actions
- modules/networking-private/vpc.tf (new) -- shared VPC, subnets, route tables, nat gateways (cloud-abstracted)
- examples/private-cluster/main.tf (modified) -- switched to new module signatures
- scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh (new) -- helper to split/rename statefiles and reassign locks
- docs/priv-deploy/state-migration.md (new) -- step-by-step migration instructions and rollback path

Snippet (gpu-node-pool/main.tf):
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu" {
  name = var.name
  instance_types = var.instance_types
  scaling_config { desired_size = var.desired_count }
  labels = merge(var.labels, {role = "gpu"})
}

Testing and CI:
- Ran terraform validate/plan against example workspaces for GCP, AWS, and Azure.
- Added unit/integration checks in pipeline that run module-level terratest suites for basic create/destroy.
- Initial CI run failed due to IAM policy being too permissive; tightened policy and re-ran. Final CI status: pass.

State migration notes:
- Because this changes the root state layout, operators must run scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh to move resources into the new env-scoped state buckets. The script supports a dry-run mode and will create backup snapshots.
- Migration steps are documented in docs/priv-deploy/state-migration.md. Recommended rollout:
  1) Dry-run in staging with snapshots enabled.
  2) Migrate one environment (lowest impact) and validate node-pool creation.
  3) Migrate remaining envs during maintenance windows.
- Rollback: the migration script keeps a snapshot which can be reapplied to restore prior state; see rollback section in docs.

Security and least-privilege:
- IAM roles created by modules/iam-private are scoped to only required KMS and S3 access. Reviewers requested and approved additional deny statements for cross-account actions.
- Added a new policy testing harness in integration tests to assert no wildcard actions on kms:Encrypt for non-admin roles.

Review conversation (high level):
- Daniel Kim: "Thanks Priya — overall this looks much cleaner. A couple of asks: tighten the EKS node IAM policy, and make subnet naming deterministic across regions."
- Priya Shah (author): "Addressed both. tightened policy in modules/iam-private/roles.tf and updated networking-private to include region-aware deterministic naming. Added tests."
- Marcel Ortega: "We should ensure state locking works with our existing consul backend in on-prem installs."
- Priya Shah: "Added a section to scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh to optionally reconfigure and test consul locks; documented required consul role in docs."
- Ava Li: "Can we keep old example workspaces working for one release cycle?"
- Priya Shah: "Yes — examples/legacy-workspace remains and is marked deprecated with explicit migration steps. We'll remove after two release cycles."

Manual testing performed:
- Provisioned a small private cluster in sandbox with GPU node pool on AWS; validated workload scheduling and node taints.
- Performed a state migration dry-run from legacy state layout to new env/<env> layout. Verified snapshots produced and that terraform plan after migration was empty for resources not changed.

Backwards compatibility:
- New modules are designed to be backwards compatible at the example-workspace level by providing transitional variables and a legacy example that maps old inputs to new ones. However, the state layout change requires explicit migration for existing customers. This is called out in release notes.

Release notes:
- Unifies Terraform state layout for private deployments to env-scoped sub-states.
- Adds gpu-node-pool, iam-private, and networking-private modules for clearer separation of concerns.
- Provides a migration script and documentation for safe upgrade.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- ENG-4523: create an automated migration runbook for large enterprises (follow-up).
- Add quota-aware autoscaling recommendations to gpu-node-pool module for Dedicated customers.

Merge: Squash merge after approvals. Changelog and docs updated, migration guide added.

If you need to reproduce locally: see docs/priv-deploy/local-development.md which includes minimal credentials and test cluster configs.
